thread:
maria-recruiter: Quick q. Raj (new hire) arrives in US this week on OPT and applied for SSN at SSA yesterday. His start date is Apr 1 and he has a valid EAD card. SSA said 2-3 weeks to receive SSN. Can we run payroll without SSN or should we defer pay until SSN arrives?

alex-peopleops: He has EAD so work authorization is fine. Main issues are payroll vendor requirements and benefits carrier SSN checks. @toni-payroll thoughts?

toni-payroll: Payroll can process pay without SSN in the vendor system if we mark "SSN applied" and use temporary placeholder. We need the SSN within 60 days to file W-2/e-file. Carrier enrollments (medical/401k) typically allow enrollment pending SSN but carriers often require SSN within 30 days — otherwise claim/payment issues may occur. We'll need candidate to sign an SSN follow-up acknowledgement.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: new-hire checklist -> collect SSN copy when available and upload to payroll secure folder. Use /hr upload-ssn.

maria-recruiter: Raj is okay to provide SSN when received. He asked whether benefits coverage will start on Apr 1 even if SSN arrives later.

toni-payroll: Yes, benefits effective date can be Apr 1 if enrollment completed by benefits deadline. We'll enroll him now and submit enrollment to carriers with SSN pending flag. If carrier rejects later, we may need to correct retroactive enrollment. No reason to withhold benefits.

anya-legal: Docs: confirm candidate has original EAD in hand and I-9 completed in-person. I-9 compliance: we can complete Section 2 with EAD + passport/other acceptable docs. SSN is not required for I-9. Keep proof of SSA receipt (stamped receipt) in file.

raj-newhire: I have the EAD and passport; SSA gave me a receipt (Form SSA-827?). I will upload scan tonight.

alex-peopleops: Good. Two payroll options: 1) Process run on Apr 15 as normal marking SSN pending; candidate paid on schedule. 2) Hold first paycheck until SSN arrives and issue retro pay after SSN — not recommended. Preference is to pay on time. Any objections?

toni-payroll: Agree pay on time. We'll process and reconcile when SSN arrives. Need candidate to complete W-4 and I-9 now. For 401(k) deferral, we can set election effective Apr 1; employer match will be applied once SSN is on record. Note: if SSN never provided, we may need to report under TIN missing — low risk if candidate provides within 60 days.

maria-recruiter: Candidate completed W-4 and signed direct-deposit. I'll upload SSA receipt and send candidate consent form for SSN follow-up.

people-ops-bot: Policy snippet: "If SSN is pending for new hires with valid authorization, proceed with payroll and benefits; require SSN within 60 calendar days. Failure to provide may result in payroll/benefit corrections." Link: https://internal.redwood/hr/ssn-policy

anya-legal: Add note — for noncitizen hires, ensure work authorization docs are retained for required retention period (3 years after hire or 1 year after employment ends, whichever is later). Also avoid using placeholder SSN on external tax filings.

alex-peopleops: Action items: @maria-recruiter - upload SSA receipt and W-4 to ticket; @raj-newhire - upload SSN when received; @toni-payroll - mark payroll record SSN-pending and enroll benefits with pending flag. I'll pre-approve any minor carrier reconciliation costs if needed.

raj-newhire: Uploaded SSA receipt. Thanks everyone. Appreciate the quick answer.

toni-payroll: Marked record in payroll as SSN-pending and queued benefits enrollment. Will confirm once carriers accept with pending flag.

alex-peopleops: Great. Closing note: do not share SSN via Slack. Use secure payroll upload. :lock:
